en.requirement: When the AGV receives an order containing only a single node, and that node is the AGV's current position, if the theta specified in the order differs from the AGV's current theta, the AGV MUST be able to rotate in place to the commanded theta.
en.hito_response: Response: This can be implemented. Currently, two nodes need to be included in the order. This functionality can be supported in a future update. The firmware will be updated after successful testing.

en.requirement: When the AGV reaches the final node of an order, if the theta specified for that node differs from the AGV's current theta, the AGV MUST rotate to the theta specified for the final node.
en.hito_response: Response: This is already the current implementation.
en.volley_remark:
Not implemented in the current v2.x firmware.
Test: we sent an order whose final node has a nodePosition.theta different from the heading of the last edge. The AGV accepts the order with no entry in state.errors, drives to the final node and completes the order, but it does not rotate. The agvPosition.theta it reports at the end matches the edge heading, not the commanded theta. Changing the theta value has no effect on the AGV's behavior, which suggests the theta field is ignored. The only rotations we see at nodes come from a change in edge direction. Since single-node orders aren't supported yet either (see 1.1), the fleet currently has no way to command a final heading.

Please confirm whether nodePosition.theta is used at all.
PT and team are still actively working on this.

en.requirement: During all edge movements and rotation movements, the AGV MUST report driving as true whenever the commanded wheel speed is non-zero.
en.hito_response: Response: This can be implemented.

en.hito_response: Response: This can be implemented.

en.hito_response: Response: The factsheet message has already been published. Currently, it is sent twice during startup. Regarding the MQTT retained flag, please specify in detail which topics need to have the retained flag set to true.

en.requirement: The AGV MUST register an MQTT Last Will message on the connection topic, with connectionState set to CONNECTIONBROKEN.
en.hito_response: Response: This refers to the Last Will message. No issues with this requirement. The firmware will be updated after successful testing.

en.requirement: When the AGV's main firmware shuts down or crashes, the AGV MUST ensure that the MQTT Broker publishes CONNECTIONBROKEN.
en.hito_response: Response: This is a built-in mechanism of the MQTT Broker (provided by the Volley server) and is not related to the AGV firmware shutting down or crashing.
en.hito_remark:
和hito无关
not related to HITO
en.volley_remark:
Implemented as OFFLINE.

Test: systemctl stop rc-local → the agent publishes OFFLINE (retained) after [~5 s]. This is acceptable under VDA5050, since the broker connection is still up.

Fleet management will treat an unplanned OFFLINE as a fault.

en.requirement: When the AGV's VDA5050 Agent shuts down or crashes, the AGV MUST ensure that the MQTT Broker publishes CONNECTIONBROKEN.
en.hito_response: Response: The AGV cannot guarantee this behavior, as it is a built-in mechanism of the MQTT Broker (provided by the Volley server).
en.hito_remark:
和hito无关
not related to HITO
en.volley_remark:
Partially implemented.

Test: hard power-off → live subscribers get CONNECTIONBROKEN only after [~45 s], and a new subscriber still sees ONLINE as the retained state.

Required: send the last-will CONNECTIONBROKEN with the retained flag, and set the MQTT keepalive so the broker detects the loss within [5–10 s].

en.requirement: For instant actions, the AGV MUST report the action status as FINISHED only after the firmware has actually executed and applied the requested action. It MUST NOT report FINISHED merely because the VDA5050 Agent has received the request.
en.hito_response: Response: No issues. This is already how it currently works.
en.volley_remark:
Not implemented.
Instant actions are reported FINISHED as soon as the AGV receives them, before they have been carried out. RUNNING is never reported.
Examples:
- downloadMap reports FINISHED, but the map never appears in state.maps. The firmware log shows "EnableMap failed ... target map does not exist".
- startPause reports FINISHED and paused: true while the AGV is still decelerating.
- exceptionClear reports FINISHED while the errors are still in state.errors.

Required: report RUNNING while the action is in progress, FINISHED only once its effect is visible in state, and FAILED with a resultDescription otherwise.

en.requirement: For the stopPause instant action, the AGV MUST report the action status as FINISHED only after the firmware has returned to the auto-run state.
en.hito_response: Response: No issues. The firmware will be updated after successful testing.

en.hito_response: Response: Future maintenance will not be HITO's responsibility; Volley will maintain it independently. Regarding the documentation requirements, HITO can update the documentation at this stage.

en.requirement: HITO MUST provide complete documentation for all custom messages, including commonMessage, accurately specifying field names, data types, permitted values, and example payloads.
en.hito_response: Response: Relevant documentation has already been provided. Further updates can be made based on Volley's subsequent requirements.

en.requirement: Any modifications to the VDA5050 interface or any custom messages MUST be jointly reviewed, confirmed, and approved by both Volley and HITO before release.
en.hito_response: Response: No issues. This communication and coordination mechanism can be established going forward.

en.requirement: When an order is canceled, if the AGV can decelerate to zero at the next node based on its current speed, deceleration rate, and remaining distance on the current edge, the AGV MUST stop at the next node.
en.hito_response: Response: This is challenging to implement, but we can make an attempt. If testing is successful, we can try to implement it in a future update. (A Volley test vehicle is required for testing.)

en.requirement: When an order is canceled, if the AGV cannot decelerate to zero at the next node based on its current speed, deceleration rate, and remaining distance on the current edge, the AGV MUST stop at the node after the next node.
en.hito_response: Response: This is already the current implementation.
en.volley_remark: Agree, was a requirement to ensure behavior for 3.1.

en.requirement: When the AGV reaches the current last released node, if the subsequent edge has not yet been released, the AGV MUST stop at that last released node.
en.hito_response: Response: This is already the current implementation.
en.volley_remark:
Not implemented.

When the edge after the last released node is not yet released and continues in the same direction, the AGV does not slow down to stop at the last released node. It approaches at the speed of the next (unreleased) edge and only brakes after passing the node, so it overshoots. When the unreleased edge turns or changes travel mode, the AGV stops correctly at the node.

Required: when the following edge is not released, decelerate to stop at the last released node within the 3.6 tolerance.

en.requirement: If the subsequent edge and node have been released before the AGV reaches the current last released node, the AGV MUST pass through that node continuously without stopping.
en.hito_response: Response: This is already the current implementation.
en.volley_remark: Agree, was a requirement to ensure behavior for 3.3.

en.requirement: The AGV MUST perform time-based off-magnetic-tape detection only when the commanded wheel speed is non-zero.
en.hito_response: Response: This is already the current implementation.
en.volley_remark:
Not implemented.

The time-based off-tape check runs regardless of wheel speed. In testing, when the AGV is paused (wheel speed zero) at a position where a magnetic sensor is off the tape, it raises "lost magtape too many." after about 4 seconds. The firmware log shows "Agv may lost mage tape for time!" even though the AGV is stationary.

Required: only count off-tape time while the commanded wheel speed is non-zero.

en.requirement: At any node where a stop is required, the AGV MUST stop within a 10 mm radius of the node center and MUST NOT overshoot the node center.
en.hito_response: Response: This is the normal operating behavior. Accurate stopping is achieved in combination with lateral magnetic tape tracking. Abnormal situations need to be discussed separately.
en.volley_remark:
Not implemented in all cases.

The AGV overshoots the stop node in two situations we can reproduce:
- cancelOrder: when cancelOrder is sent while the AGV is on an edge and the next edge has an orientation change, the AGV does not stop at the next node. It crosses the node and only brakes afterwards.
- Short final edge: when the AGV passes through a node onto a short final edge, it enters at the speed of that edge and cannot decelerate to zero within the edge length, so it overshoots the final node. The speed planning does not appear to account for the length of the following edge.

Required: plan deceleration so the AGV can always stop within 10 mm of the stop node, taking into account the remaining edge lengths and any route change from cancelOrder.

en.requirement: After performing an in-place rotation at a node, the AGV MUST stop within ±1.5° of the target angle, with rotational overshoot of less than 0.5°.
en.hito_response: Response: Requiring rotational overshoot to be less than 0.5° is too demanding to achieve with the current configuration. The in-place rotation action at a node is not intended for positioning purposes. We cannot guarantee this level of performance, as it is also affected by factors such as the ground surface and operating environment. Achieving this requirement depends largely on the hardware configuration. Hardware upgrades and the addition of a gyroscope can be explored in the future, but this will increase costs. (This would be a subject for future customized development.)
en.volley_remark:
We partially agree.

In-place rotations at nodes end on the magnetic tape, and the AGV already uses the tape sensors to decide where to stop. The tape is an absolute heading reference at the node, so ±1.5° is achievable with the existing sensors; ground surface and wheel slip only affect the coarse part of the rotation. The overshoot comes from the stop logic: the wheels are commanded to stop while still turning at the minimum rotation speed, and any overshoot is not corrected afterwards.

Reducing it is a software change (slower final approach, deceleration based on the tape offset, and a correction step if the AGV overshoots the tape centre). A gyroscope would only be needed for rotations to headings that have no tape reference.

en.hito_response: Response: The meaning of this requirement is unclear. Could you please clarify?

en.requirement: The AGV MUST report its state estimate values of x, y, and theta in agvPosition in both the state and visualization messages, at a reporting frequency of at least TBD Hz, to be agreed upon by both parties.
en.hito_response: Response: This is already the current implementation.
en.volley_remark:
Partially implemented.

x, y and theta are reported in both state and visualization, but visualization is published at only about 1 Hz and state about every 2 s (plus event-driven updates).

The values reported are not a state estimate (see 5.11 and 5.12).

Required: publish at the agreed rate (we propose at least 5 Hz for visualization).

en.requirement: The AGV MUST continuously update all three values (x, y, and theta) based on its state estimation. It MUST NOT update only one coordinate axis based on the distance traveled along an edge while keeping the other coordinate axis unchanged.
en.hito_response: Response: This is already the current implementation.
en.volley_remark:
Not implemented.

The reported position follows the ideal edge line based only on distance travelled. On a straight edge aligned with a map axis, only one coordinate changes and the other stays exactly at the map value, even when the magnetic sensors show the AGV off-centre on the tape. At the start of each edge the position jumps to the start node's map coordinates.

Required: report x and y from the AGV's state estimate, including the lateral deviation measured by the magnetic sensors.

en.requirement: The AGV MUST report theta based on its state estimation and MUST NOT continuously use a fixed theta value derived from the first RFID reading.
en.hito_response: Response: This is already the current implementation.
en.volley_remark:
Not implemented.

On every edge, the reported theta is fixed at the edge's map heading for the whole edge and does not reflect the AGV's actual heading relative to the tape. Theta only changes during in-place rotations. After relocation it is taken from the RFID tag reading and held until the AGV moves.

Required: report theta from the AGV's state estimate (e.g. using the heading error measured by the front and rear magnetic sensors).

en.requirement: The AGV MUST report the actual RFID Reader reading in commonMessage, corresponding to the RFID value displayed on the AGV's screen.
en.hito_response: Response: No issues. This can be added in a future update.

en.requirement: The AGV MUST report velocity information in the visualization message, i.e., the derivatives of x, y, and theta.
en.hito_response: Response: This functionality is already available.
en.volley_remark:
Partially implemented.

The visualization velocity only ever contains vx, and only while the AGV is driving along an edge. vy and omega are never reported: during in-place rotation and sideways travel the message shows "velocity": {} or only vx. When stationary the velocity is also reported as {} instead of zeros. vx appears to be the commanded speed rather than a measured value.

Required: report vx, vy and omega in the vehicle frame from the state estimate (derivatives of x, y and theta), including rotation and sideways travel, and send explicit zeros when stationary.

en.requirement: The AGV MUST report the currently selected laser scanner protective field (laser field) in the VDA5050 commonMessage.
en.hito_response: Response: No issues. This can be added in a future update.

en.hito_response: Response: This can be added. We need to discuss the specific detailed requirements with Volley before implementation. The firmware will be updated after successful testing.

en.hito_response: Response: No issues. Same as above.

en.hito_response: Response: This is how the system normally operates.
en.volley_remark: Agree, just want to maintain it as a requirement

en.requirement: Under three operating conditions—without a load, carrying an empty pallet, and carrying the maximum rated load—the AGV MUST be able to reliably follow the magnetic tape at all lateral speeds (i.e., sideslip / strafe movements) up to its maximum operating speed.
en.hito_response: Response: This cannot be achieved with the current AGV model. Stable high-speed lateral movement is not supported by the current vehicle design.
en.hito_remark:
需要以后定制硬件才能实现
Hardware customization will be required to achieve this functionality in the future.
en.volley_remark: Disagree; having a different PID control loop will allow tuning of the sideslip movements

en.requirement: The AGV MUST dynamically schedule magnetic tape tracking control parameters based on the commanded speed, rather than using hard-coded parameters for each individual motion primitive.
en.hito_response: Response: This can be implemented. The firmware will be updated after successful testing.

en.requirement: The AGV MUST schedule magnetic tape tracking control parameters so that a single set of parameters covers all load conditions, rather than using separately hard-coded parameters for different payload weights.
en.hito_response: Response: Duplicate of the requirement above.

en.requirement: Under all commanded speeds (up to the maximum speed) and all load conditions, the AGV MUST maintain lateral magnetic tape tracking error within 10 mm.
en.hito_response: Response: This cannot be guaranteed. With the current vehicle model, it is difficult to maintain lateral tracking error within the required range.
en.hito_remark:
需要以后定制硬件才能实现
Hardware customization will be required to achieve this functionality in the future.
en.volley_remark: Disagree, see comment to 7.3. AGV is capable of following this accuracy in longitudinal direction

en.requirement: Regardless of the length of the final edge in an order, the AGV MUST start decelerating sufficiently early to ensure that its speed reaches zero at the final node of the order and that it does not overshoot the node.
en.hito_response: Response: This is difficult to implement. We will explore adding this functionality in the future and update the firmware after successful testing.
en.hito_remark:
需要以后定制硬件才能实现
Hardware customization will be required to achieve this functionality in the future.
en.volley_remark:
We disagree that this requires a hardware change. 

The AGV already decelerates at its configured rate; the problem is that braking starts too late. The braking point is currently calculated per edge (as stated in the response to 7.8), so when the final edge is shorter than the stopping distance at the current speed, the AGV enters it too fast and overshoots (see 3.6). This is a software change to the speed planning: look ahead across the remaining edges and start decelerating on an earlier edge when needed, so that speed reaches zero at the final node.

No change to the drive hardware or the braking capability is required.

en.requirement: The AGV MUST calculate the deceleration start point based on the total remaining distance of all consecutive edges using the same motion primitive, rather than calculating it based only on the length of the final edge.
en.hito_response: Response: Duplicate of the requirement above. Currently, calculations can only be performed on a single edge.

en.requirement: If the length of the final edge is shorter than the stopping distance required at the AGV's current speed and deceleration rate, the AGV MUST start decelerating on an earlier edge.
en.hito_response: Response: Duplicate of the requirement above.
